SOUTH AFRICA  This look channels the traditional stylings of the Sotho tribe, with accessories inspired by those worn by the women of the Ndebele tribe, specifically the Dzilla.  TUNISIA  A nod to the intricately layered and voluminous traditional clothing worn by Tunisian women, as well as the embellished headdresses worn more often by women in the south. IVORY COAST  The shape of this look channels the volume of a traditional Ivorian garment called the boubou, which is also worn across west Africa. Japan's most famous Katsudon🍚  If you’ve never had this, you are missing out on one of Japan’s greatest masterpieces. It’s a crispy, golden pork cutlet (Tonkatsu) simmered in a sweet and savory dashi broth with tender onions and silky, marbled eggs—all piled high on a steaming bowl of rice. It’s crunchy, juicy, sweet, savory, and pure perfection in every single bite! 🛒 The Ingredients The Crunch: Pork loin chop breaded in crispy Japanese Panko. The Umami Broth: Dashi stock, soy sauce, mirin, and a pinch of sugar. The Topping: Thinly sliced yellow onions and lightly beaten eggs. The Base: Steamed Japanese short-grain rice. 🍳 How It’s Made (The Process) Fry: Season and coat the pork in flour, egg, and panko. Deep fry until golden brown and slice it up. Simmer: Cook the onions in the savory dashi broth until tender. Assemble: Lay the crispy katsu right on top of the onions, pour the swirled eggs around it, and cover until softly set.
